en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: The 400 runs straight from {city} into the Greater Toronto Area, and that single fact causes most of the waste I find in {city} accounts. A radius drawn generously around the city reaches south into Vaughan and beyond, where the auction is priced by advertisers with national budgets. You end up paying Toronto rates to reach people who were never going to drive to {city}, and the report shows a rising cost per click that nobody can explain. Tightening the geography is usually the first and cheapest fix available here.

The same corridor causes a subtler problem. A large share of {city} residents work in the GTA, which means for eight hours a day your customers are physically inside a different search market, seeing a different set of competitors, and searching on a phone that thinks it is in Toronto. If your ad schedule and your targeting both assume the customer is in {city} when they are looking, you are absent for a good part of the day they are actually deciding.

None of that makes {city} a satellite of Toronto. Local demand is real and growing at 8.0%, well above the national rate, and in {industries} the customer genuinely wants somebody local. The plan just has to be built by someone who knows the corridor is there, rather than by copying either a Toronto playbook or a small-town one.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account. If you want someone who will walk into your shop, I am the wrong hire and I will say so on the call rather than after you have paid.

faq.q: Why is our cost per click so much higher than we expected?
faq.a: In {city} the usual cause is a targeting radius that reaches down the 400 into the Greater Toronto Area. The auction there is priced by advertisers with far bigger budgets, and once your campaign overlaps it those prices become your prices. It is one of the few problems in this business that can be fixed in an afternoon.

faq.q: Should we advertise in Toronto as well?
faq.a: Only if you can actually serve customers there and they have a reason to choose you over somebody closer to them. For most {city} businesses the answer is no, and the more useful move is to stop accidentally advertising there while pretending not to.

faq.q: Our customers commute. Does that change anything?
faq.a: It changes when and where they search, which affects your ad schedule and your geographic targeting more than your message. It also raises the value of organic and AI visibility, because those reach the customer regardless of which market their phone thinks it is in at the time.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
